title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to a Kobalos malware infection in a high-performance computing environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are a cybersecurity analyst responding to an alert about suspicious activity on the target host. The target host is part of a high-performance computing cluster running Ubuntu. Initial analysis suggests the presence of the Kobalos malware, a complex backdoor that targets HPC clusters. Your goal is to investigate the infection, identify the scope, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: SSH access to the target host (192.168.50.5) as user cyrano with password cyrano. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the word 'start' to proceed to the next level.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious service running on the target host
levels.content: Investigate running services on the target host. Identify any suspicious or unexpected services. The name of the suspicious service is the flag.
levels.solution: Check systemd services and look for any services related to payload transfer or check-in.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd services can be listed using the systemctl command. Look for any services that seem out of place or related to malicious activity.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all services and look for any services related to payload transfer or check-in.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all services and identify the suspicious one.

levels.title: Investigate the suspicious outbound connection
levels.content: Analyze network connections from the target host. Identify any suspicious outbound connections. The destination port of the suspicious outbound connection is the flag.
levels.solution: Check the systemd timer and service files for the suspicious service.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network connections can be analyzed using the ss command. Look for any connections that seem suspicious or unexpected.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the ss command to list all network connections and look for any outbound connections that seem suspicious.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections and identify the suspicious outbound connection.

levels.title: Contain the C2 communication
levels.content: Based on your previous findings, contain the C2 communication. The port number used to contain the communication is the flag.
levels.solution: Use firewall rules to block the identified port.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Firewall rules can be used to block network traffic. Look for any rules that can block the suspicious port.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the iptables command to create a firewall rule that blocks the identified port.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run the command 'iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 7070 -j DROP' to block the suspicious port.
